en.title: Modern Warfare 4 Tackles Wallhacks With 'Server Culling' Tech
en.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is introducing a new anti-cheat system called 'server culling' to combat wallhacks. This innovative technology aims to make matches fairer by limiting the information players receive, potentially eradicating a long-standing issue for the franchise.
en.body:
The perennial battle against cheaters in the **Call of Duty** franchise may be taking a significant turn with the upcoming **Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4**. Developer Infinity Ward and publisher Activision have unveiled a new anti-cheat measure, dubbed "server culling," designed to tackle the pervasive problem of wallhacks head-on. This system promises to make the battlefield a more honest place for players on **PlayStation 5**, **XBOX Series X|S**, and PC when the game launches on October 23, 2026.

For years, wallhacks have allowed unscrupulous players to gain an unfair advantage by seeing enemy positions through solid surfaces. This exploit relies on game servers sharing player location data with all connected clients, even when those players are hidden from view. However, **Modern Warfare 4**'s "server culling" aims to fundamentally alter this by building occlusion layers directly into the game's environments. Essentially, the game's backend will only transmit information about players that are actually visible to you on screen. If you can't see an enemy behind a wall, the server won't tell anyone else they're there, effectively blindfolding wallhackers and leveling the playing field.

"With **Modern Warfare 4**, we’re introducing a new way to fight back: Server Culling," the official **Call of Duty** social media channels announced, accompanied by a video detailing the new system. This move addresses a core frustration for many fans who feel that cheating detracts from the core experience. The emphasis on refined visual effects and improved enemy visibility in the campaign and multiplayer modes also suggests a broader commitment to ensuring fair play and authentic combat.

## A Fairer Fight for All

The implications of "server culling" extend beyond just eliminating wallhacks. By ensuring that information is strictly tied to what players can visually confirm, the system could also bolster the integrity of other competitive mechanics. Coupled with a rebuilt recoil and weapon handling system that aims for more direct player input and predictability, **Modern Warfare 4** is shaping up to be a title that prioritizes genuine skill and tactical awareness. The campaign, which plunges players into a world threatened by North Korea's invasion, also promises immersive combat scenarios, but it's the multiplayer's potential for a cleaner experience that has the community buzzing.

## What's Next

**Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4** is slated for release on October 23, 2026. Players can anticipate a campaign exploring global conflict and a multiplayer suite that appears poised to set a new standard for fairness in the series. Further details on specific multiplayer modes and features are expected in the lead-up to launch.

content_raw: Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4 , Activision has a plan to change that. If you're unfamiliar with the term, wallhacks are a type of cheat that allows nefarious players to see their opponents' every move through walls. Call of Duty is far from the only multiplayer-centric gaming franchise to suffer from cheaters who use the tool, but it might be the most infamous example – and in Modern Warfare 4, that's all about to change. As detailed in a new video published on the franchise's official social media pages, publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward revealed a new system aimed at combating wallhack cheaters. Called "server culling," the goal is to make Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 more reliable – and fair – than ever before. Few things ruin a great match faster than wondering whether an opponent earned the win or saw you through a wall. Wallhacks give cheaters information they were never meant to have. With Modern Warfare 4, we’re introducing a new way to fight back: Server Culling. Here’s how it… pic.twitter.com/62m41zMbLa — Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) October 2, 2026 The relatively in-depth explanation touches on how cheaters have been able to use wallhacks thus far. Usually, servers share information, such as a player's in-game location, between game clients. It means that, even when you can't see an enemy hiding behind cover, waiting to pop out for an easy kill, the game itself still recognizes that the player is there. Server culling, which saw Infinity Ward build occlusion layers into Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's environments, essentially limits information to what the player is able to see. So, if you can't see someone behind the wall, the backend can't either – and that goes for wallhackers, too. "For legitimate players, the match plays exactly as intended," Activision explained. "For cheat developers, this creates a major new obstacle." Server culling will touch every multiplayer map available in Modern Warfare 4 when launch arrives, but it doesn't stop there. Call of Duty's new take on DMZ, the Combat Outpost mode, Warzone, and future updates will benefit from this attack on wallhacks, too. All of this new tech works alongside pre-existing anti-cheat methods across all platforms , too. Activision said it expects server culling to "disturb the cheat marketplace," but it won't "sit on our hands" when it comes to improving the overall experience going forward. There are plenty of different ways for cheaters to disrupt the experience for the average player, and while cheat manufacterers will no doubt look for new ways to learn from Activision's advancements, the publisher said it will do its best to stay on top of the issue. "Cheat software can’t reveal information it never receives," the Call of Duty team explained in a follow-up post .
